result.title: A Unified Interpretable Semantic Framework for Multi-Modal Fiber Sensing Under Data Scarcity
result.summary: We propose a unified interpretable semantic framework for multi-modal fiber sensing under data scarcity. The framework maps heterogeneous measurements from state of-polarization (SOP) monitoring, distributed acoustic sensing (DAS), and optical time-domain reflectometry (OTDR) into a shared set of physics-grounded semantic descriptors capturing impulsiveness, persistence, structural characteristics, and energy concentration. Inference is performed through reasoning over semantic class profiles, optionally assisted by retrieval of semantically similar examples to resolve ambiguity and support adaptation without model retraining. Experimental validation on real SOP, DAS, and OTDR datasets demonstrates robust performance across sensing modalities, achieving accuracies of 95.0%, 91.1%, and 94.6%, respectively, while providing transparent and physically interpretable decisions. The proposed framework establishes a unified and data efficient approach for optical fiber sensing in evolving and data scarce deployment environments.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向光纤多模态传感（SOP、DAS、OTDR）的统一可解释语义框架：将异构测量映射为物理语义描述子，再基于语义类别剖面与相似样例检索进行推理分类，在数据稀缺下报告约 91%–95% 的准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作面向光纤传感信号分类，其「推理」仅为人工物理描述子与类别剖面匹配及样例检索，不涉及 VLM 内部表示、latent 状态生成或视觉证据使用，与本主线无实质联系，也没有可供核查的方法线索。
